summary: Lewis County, NY tower built in 1928 near Number Four, closed in the early 1980s and removed in 1987; its upper section now stands at the DEC Lowville demonstration area.

facts.design: Aermotor LX25 steel tower with ladders between the landings at first, later stairs; glass-enclosed observatory
facts.status_note: Only the upper section stands, at the DEC Lowville Forestry Demonstration Area; only the tower footers remain at the original Number Four site
facts.agency: Fisher Forestry and Realty Company (built 1928); NYS Conservation Department (operated from 1945)

events.note: Fisher Forestry and Realty Company erected the steel tower with Conservation Department co-operation; sources give 75, 80 and 90 feet for its height
Conservation Department took over operation from the landowner; the duties of the Beaver Lake Mountain lookout moved to Number Four
Observer's cabin and standard stairs added, per a 2019 post quoted in the 2023 newsletter; Wikipedia dates the ladder-to-stair change to about 1960
Land with the cabin and tower transferred from the landowner to New York State
Final year of operation; operations discontinued
Observer's cabin moved to Nicks Lake Campground, around 1984
Tower removed from the original site; the chief reason cited was extensive vandalism
Upper section moved to and displayed at the DEC Lowville Forestry Demonstration Area; date not given
A 2018 visit account by Bill Hill, quoted in the 2023 newsletter, says the tower was shortened to 25 feet; no other source read mentions this

corrections.current: The lookout was moved to Lowville Demonstration Forest.
corrections.proposed: Only the upper section was moved, to the DEC Lowville Forestry Demonstration Area. The rest of the tower was removed in 1987; only tower footers remain at Number Four.
corrections.why: The record implies the whole tower moved; the DEC and Wikipedia describe only the upper section moving, and the rest was removed from the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 75 feet (Wikipedia; Bill Hill's 2018 visit account quoted in the newsletter), about 80 feet (July 1928 newspapers) and 90 feet (DEC). No height is recorded.
The newsletter quotes a 2019 post that dates the ladders-to-stairs change to 1945; Wikipedia says around 1960. Both are kept as dated claims.
The DEC says the upper section was displayed near the area's entrance; Wikipedia says it was used to build a demonstration tower beside the DEC office. Both may be true; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The original site and the moved upper section are both covered, because the record's status is relocated. Sources disagree on height (75, about 80, 90 feet) and on the stair date (1945 in a 2019 post quoted by the newsletter, around 1960 in Wikipedia); the record carries no height. The 'shortened to 25 feet' figure comes from a 2018 visit account by Bill Hill, quoted in the newsletter, and is reported as a visitor's claim. No access level is recorded for the original site: the DEC page covers only Lowville, and the newsletter describes a campsite near the old site without stating rules. The sibling record us-ny-number-four-at-lowville-demonstration-forest covers the Lowville tower itself.
